title: The reduction's vectors order by order, on the cut-open torus at powers of two
claim: Pre-registered 2026-11-10, before the proof attempt. At n = 2^m, h = n/2, q = 2n, for a in GF(q)* with G the monic least-degree element of ker X_b, k = h - deg G, J = ceil(k/2), N = G(k) G(k + 1) and the family Zhat(l) of CHAIN-ORDERS-20261110-001A (Theorem 4): to be found, order by order, closed forms of the vectors psi_r of the reduction of Zhat to ker X_b = G F[Y]_(<J), in the theta-picture theta_r = psi_r/G where the chain equations read Tr theta_r = tau theta_(r-1) + (the family's high terms) mod k^h (Tr = 1 + tau in characteristic 2), and from them, by the 2n + 1 rule, the reduction's coefficient at l^(2t-1) on co-distance t = k - i - j. Target: that coefficient is [t a power of two] (G monic) and every lower coefficient vanishes, at every t; with CHAIN-ORDERS-20261110-001A's Theorem 3 this is the chain lemma at every order. Frozen stop rule: the first order r >= 2 for which no closed form of psi_r is found (an explicit formula verified exactly at every a for sides 8 to 64) ends the attempt, and the record states the leading form proved through the co-distance that order reaches.
failure_conditions: An order r and an eigenvalue at which a claimed closed form of psi_r fails, or the reduction's coefficient at l^(2t-1) on co-distance t differs from [t a power of two] (computed false at every a for sides 8 to 256 by CHAIN-ORDERS-20261110-001).
remaining_obligations: closed forms of psi_2, psi_3, ... and the leading form at each co-distance, or the first order with no closed form
foundation_claim_scope: The square torus of rule-60 rings with equally spaced law-(12, 12) contacts, cut open by a ring of cuts each way (A30, A32, A37, A38); its walk over GF(2), at sides 2^m. The spectrum is a contact-level reading, so it does not depend on how the rings are declared (A45).

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the coordinator's go-ahead on 2026-11-10 (sub-goals B73 and B91).
validation.status: pre-registered; the proof attempt to follow
